subject: Private deployment: custody, egress & BYOK clarifications
messages:
From: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@blueharbor.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: custody, egress & BYOK clarifications

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the demo last week. BlueHarbor is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for our NLP PHI redaction pipeline. Legal & infosec have a few open items we need clarified before we move to procurement:

- We need a clear statement of custody for customer-controlled keys (BYOK) and whether Redwood or any operator can unseal keys.
- Operator access: what activities require operator credentials, and do you have a break-glass process we can rely on?
- Data egress: any automated telemetry, crash dumps, or model snapshots that could include customer data — how are those handled and where are they stored?
- Cross-border transfers: what data flows exist between Redwood control-plane and customer VPC/on-prem instances?

Can you share a short annex/summary we can attach to our DPA and a sample operator access matrix? Procurement is also asking for an approximate timeline for any required escrow/escape clauses.

Thanks,
Alyssa Kim
Head of Procurement
BlueHarbor Health

Attachments: none

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@blueharbor.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment: custody, egress & BYOK clarifications

Alyssa — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Appreciated the clear list.

Short answers up front: yes, BYOK is supported and keys are customer-controlled; Redwood operators do not have routine ability to unseal customer CMKs. We will send a short annex that spells the operational assumptions and propose an operator access matrix for your review.

Next steps I propose:
- Attached: Redwood-Private-DPA-Annex-v1.pdf (summary of custody, data flows, egress controls)
- Attached: operator-access-matrix.xlsx (roles, allowed activities, break-glass triggers)
- Internal: I’ve looped in Irene (security) for technical details and Karthik for deployment sequencing and timeline.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call early next week to walk the annex with your security and legal teams?

Thanks,
Logan Wright

logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0182

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@blueharbor.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: custody, egress & BYOK clarifications

Logan / Alyssa — quick technical clarifications from BlueHarbor SecOps: 

1) HSM vs software-wrapped keys: Does Redwood Private support external HSMs (Cloud HSM / on-prem HSM) for CMK wrapping, or is it software-managed only? If HSM is supported, where are keys backed up and what are the escrow options?

2) Operator break-glass: what exact logs are generated during a break-glass event and how long are they retained? Who signs off on an operator-initiated key unseal?

3) Telemetry & crash data: any automated telemetry that contains partial request payloads (stacks, sample inputs) — is that redacted by default? Where is that telemetry stored (redwood cloud region)?

4) Cross-border: will any customer metadata (request id, timestamps, customer tenant id) be sent to Redwood control-plane outside the US for routing or billing?

Also, can you provide SOC 2 type II evidence and the latest penetration test summary for the Private runtime? We can provisionally proceed on the call, but procurement will want this evidence before signing.

Thanks,
Marcus Lee
Sr. Security Engineer, BlueHarbor Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@blueharbor.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: custody, egress & BYOK clarifications

Marcus — thanks for the detailed items. I pulled together concise responses and a short proposed clause you can drop into a DPA addendum. Summary answers first:

- HSM support: Redwood Private supports both customer-supplied HSMs (on-prem or cloud HSMs where supported) and software-wrapped BYOK. When customers supply an HSM, Redwood never holds the unwrapped key material. Backup/escrow of keys remains with the customer unless an explicit escrow arrangement is requested and documented.

- Operator break-glass: Operator access is gated by a documented break-glass policy. Break-glass events require two-person approval (senior SRE + security lead), and the action is fully logged with immutable audit entries (operator identity, JIRA ticket ref, reason, commands issued). Logs retained for 365 days by default; we can negotiate extended retention.

- Telemetry: By default, telemetry excludes full request payloads. Stack traces and crash dumps are sanitized; sampling of anonymized metrics is stored in Redwood-hosted telemetry (US regions). We can configure telemetry redaction to strip identifiers on customer request.

- Control-plane metadata: Minimal metadata (request id, model name, routing decision) is sent to Redwood control plane for orchestration and billing. No customer input data or PHI is transmitted. Control-plane endpoints for Private customers can be restricted to US regions only.

Proposed DPA addendum clause (suggestion — feel free to redline):
"Customer Key Custody and Operator Access. Customer shall retain sole control of Customer Master Keys (CMKs). Redwood shall not possess, store, or be able to derive the plaintext of Customer CMKs unless expressly authorized via a documented, auditable, and time-limited break-glass process. Break-glass may only be initiated following two-person authorization documented in Company incident procedures, and all actions shall be recorded in immutable audit logs retained for a minimum of 365 days. Redwood shall not extract or retain customer input data in crash dumps or telemetry; any telemetry transmitted to Redwood is sanitized to remove PHI and customer identifiers by default."

Attachments: redwood-byok-clauses.txt (plain text with clause examples)

Happy to walk through the annex on a call — I can also share sample SOC2 report excerpts and a redacted pen-test summary under NDA.

--
Irene Choi
Director, Product Security
Irene.Choi@redwood.com

Subject: DPA addendum draft and mutual action plan

Alyssa — attaching a DPA addendum draft that incorporates the BYOK / operator access language Irene suggested and a short mutual action plan so procurement has visibility on timeline.

Key items in the draft:
- BYOK preservation clause and explicit prohibition on Redwood deriving plaintext CMKs without break-glass.
- Operator access matrix cross-referenced as Annex A (operator-access-matrix.xlsx).
- Telemetry redaction and proof evidence requirement (SOC 2 excerpts + pen-test summary to be shared under NDA).
- Data flow diagram & control-plane endpoint restriction to US (Annex B).

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) Week 1: BlueHarbor legal to review draft and return redlines (target by 2027-03-18).
2) Week 2: Joint SecOps call to review technical controls and break-glass flow (schedule by 2027-03-22).
3) Week 3: Redwood provides redacted SOC2 excerpts and pen-test summary under NDA; procurement to start master services agreement redlines.

Please redline the attached docx and we’ll iterate. If you prefer, we can open a shared Google Doc and enable comments.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

We’ll aim to return redlines on the DPA draft by Friday (2027-03-18) and confirm availability for the SecOps call next week. Also please send the NDA for SOC2 artifacts so we can expedite review.
